notes: Deterministic ciq_facts.json cross-check (step 1c) was NOT available for this run and could not be generated in this environment: the environment's only Python interpreter is 3.9.6, and .claude/tools/ciq.py requires enum.StrEnum (Python >=3.11); no newer interpreter is installed (checked /usr/local/opt/python@3.11/3.12/3.13 — cellar formulas not actually installed). This is noted per the tool's own best-effort/skip instruction, not treated as a run defect. In its place, this audit ran the deterministic resolve_citations.py resolver plus extensive direct corpus greps and manual cross-module tracing for every material claim. Two tool-behavior notes for future audits of this run: (1) resolve_citations.py's regex uses a negative lookbehind that excludes any match immediately preceded by a minus sign, producing false-negative hit_count=0 for figures stored in the pool as negative cash-flow-statement outflows (e.g. Quest's -982.1 acquisition cash outflow) — these were confirmed present via direct grep, not treated as unsupported; (2) several figures (150.0, 6.00, 200.0) recur across many unrelated contexts in the pool (loan repayments, historical facility sizes, buyback authorizations), so the resolver's raw hit_count alone is insufficient — each was manually disambiguated to its cited specific context. Overall the dossier's rating-driving numbers (OWYN write-off, cumulative impairment total, net debt/leverage, EV bridge, scenario math, governance-score formula, consensus target) are well-sourced and tie out. The two real defects found — an unsupported $124.0M Atkins-impairment component figure isolated to earnings/01_historical-financials.md (not propagated to headline numbers), and a repeated ~60bps overstatement of the five-year gross-margin decline (~800bps stated vs 740bps from the module's own cited endpoints) — do not change the OWYN/RF-CAP-004 rating cap or the scenario/valuation math, so they do not rise to Material. A low-severity, unreconciled $0.2M cross-module discrepancy on the OWYN purchase price ($280.2M vs $280.4M, both genuinely sourced to different document types) and a period/scope-mismatched juxtaposition of the $391.9M cumulative impairment against a FY2025-only 56.3% adjustment ratio round out the findings.
